questions.stem: The Supreme Court Rules, 2013 were framed under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 145 is the enabling provision under which the Supreme Court may make rules for regulating its practice and procedure.

questions.stem: The Supreme Court Rules, 2013 came into force on:
questions.explanation: The Rules were notified on 27 May 2014 (G.S.R. 368(E)) and came into force on 19 August 2014, appointed by the CJI by notification.
questions.sourceRef: Supreme Court Rules, 2013 — citation and commencement

questions.stem: The Supreme Court Rules, 2013 are divided into:
options: Parts I–IV and Orders I–LVI, with Forms appended
questions.explanation: The Rules are structured as Part I (General) through Part IV, divided into Orders I–LVI, with Forms appended. They replaced the Supreme Court Rules, 1966.

questions.stem: Under Order I rule 2 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013, the expression 'Court appealed from' includes:
options: a Tribunal or any other judicial body from which an appeal is preferred to the Court
any court subordinate to a High Court
questions.explanation: 'Court appealed from' includes a Tribunal or any other judicial body from which an appeal is preferred to the Court — the definition is inclusive, not exhaustive.
questions.sourceRef: Supreme Court Rules, 2013, Order I r.2

questions.stem: To qualify as an advocate-on-record under Order IV rule 5, an advocate must have been on the roll of a State Bar Council for at least:
questions.explanation: Order IV r.5 requires the name to be on a State Bar Council roll for at least four years as on the commencement of training, plus one year's training and passing the AoR examination.
questions.sourceRef: Supreme Court Rules, 2013, Order IV r.5

questions.stem: Under the Supreme Court Rules, 2013, the summer vacation of the Court shall not exceed:
questions.explanation: Order II provides that the summer vacation shall not exceed seven weeks, and total vacation plus holidays shall not exceed 103 days.

questions.stem: The total of vacations and holidays of the Supreme Court shall not exceed:
questions.explanation: Order II caps the total of vacation and holidays at 103 days, excluding Sundays that do not fall within a vacation.

questions.stem: Under the Supreme Court Rules, 2013, the custody of the records of the Court is with:
questions.explanation: Order III provides that the Secretary General has custody of the records of the Court, and keeps the official seal.

questions.stem: A senior advocate is designated under:
options: Order IV rule 5 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013
s.7 of the Bar Councils Act
questions.explanation: The Rules define a senior advocate as one designated under s.16(2) of the Advocates Act, 1961.
questions.sourceRef: Supreme Court Rules, 2013, Order I r.2

questions.stem: Under the Supreme Court Rules, 2013, the expression 'Judge' means:
options: a Judge of the Supreme Court
any judicial officer of a court in India
a Judge of a High Court only
the Chief Justice of India only
questions.explanation: Order I r.2 defines 'Judge' as a Judge of the Court, i.e. the Supreme Court. 'Court' means the Supreme Court of India.
questions.sourceRef: Supreme Court Rules, 2013, Order I r.2

questions.stem: On Saturdays, the offices of the Supreme Court are open from 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., and no work is admitted after:
questions.explanation: Order II provides that offices open on Saturdays from 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., with no work admitted after 12 noon unless urgent. The Court does not ordinarily sit on Saturdays.

questions.stem: An advocate enrolled for less than one year on a State Bar Council roll may, under the Supreme Court Rules, 2013:
options: only mention matters and not argue them
argue matters but not file appearances
do everything an advocate-on-record may do
questions.explanation: Order IV allows an advocate enrolled for less than one year to only mention matters (time, date, adjournment) and not argue; only an advocate-on-record may act or file an appearance.

questions.stem: Under Order I rule 2 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013, the expression 'respondent' includes:
questions.explanation: The definition of 'respondent' includes an intervener — a classic 'includes' trap where the listed item extends, not restricts, the meaning.
questions.sourceRef: Supreme Court Rules, 2013, Order I r.2

questions.stem: Under the Supreme Court Rules, 2013, an 'advocate' means a person whose name is entered on the roll of advocates prepared and maintained by:
options: a State Bar Council under the Advocates Act, 1961
questions.explanation: An 'advocate' is one whose name is on the roll prepared and maintained by a State Bar Council under the Advocates Act, 1961.
questions.sourceRef: Supreme Court Rules, 2013, Order I r.2

questions.stem: Under the Supreme Court Rules, 2013, the expression 'Chief Justice' includes:
options: a Judge appointed under Article 126 to perform the duties of the Chief Justice
the Chief Justice of any High Court
the senior-most puisne Judge of the Supreme Court
the Chief Justice of India only
questions.explanation: 'Chief Justice' means the Chief Justice of India and includes a Judge appointed under Article 126 to perform the duties of the office of the Chief Justice.
questions.sourceRef: Supreme Court Rules, 2013, Order I r.2

questions.stem: The Supreme Court Rules, 2013 replaced the:
questions.explanation: The 2013 Rules repealed and replaced the earlier Supreme Court Rules, 1966.
